title: vendored_paths, vendored_dir_files and doctor's unowned check swallow find's errors, so a directory find cannot read vendors a project short, or ends upgrade in silence
body:
FOUND by cc's critic-shell review of issue 0113's build on 2026-09-23, and then driven by cc at 0113's build through every command that reaches it. Line numbers are at 0113's landing.

`vendored_paths` (lib/install:262) enumerates devbin's vendored half with `find "$lib" -type f 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort | while ...; done`, then `return 0`. find's stderr goes to /dev/null, neither its status nor the pipeline's is read, and the function returns 0 however much find could not see. So the `|| return 1` at its caller, `paths="$(vendored_paths "$srcroot")" || return 1` (lib/install:867), can never fire.

DRIVEN, in a devbin source tree with `lib/pages` at mode 000. What happens depends on how the caller reads the list:
- `install --into <project>` from that source vendors 45 of the 60 files and exits 0. The project gets no lib/pages/, so from 0113 on every `help <built-in>` there says devbin ships no page, which is false. The vendoring loop reads the list inside a heredoc, where the failure is invisible.
- `upgrade --from` that source, in a project, exits 1 and prints nothing at all. Under the handler's errexit and pipefail the failed find ends the list's command substitution, and find's stderr was sent to /dev/null, so nobody is told why. Nothing is removed.
- Publishing from it is refused, and by a gate that works: the dirty-tree gate's seam line reports `seam: UNREADABLE`. Plain `git status --porcelain` cannot see into the directory, but seam_state_of can. So the harm the review inferred, a short install whose consumers then delete their intact copies, is not reachable through publish.
The trigger, an unreadable directory in devbin's source, is rare. The class is that a list comes back short, or a command dies, with nothing said.

THE SAME SHAPE, at two more sites:
- vendored_dir_files (lib/install:281), same pipeline;
- doctor's _check_unowned (lib/cmd/doctor:286), `$(find "$DEVBIN_LIB" -type f 2>/dev/null | LC_ALL=C sort)` inside a heredoc. There a file doctor cannot list is a file it never reports as unowned.

FIX: take find's output and status into a variable first, `files="$(find "$lib" -type f)" || return 1`, leaving stderr visible, then sort and format from the variable. Each site gets an arm that makes a directory unreadable and sees the refusal, plus a control that the readable tree still lists everything. A mode-000 directory is readable by root, so each arm skips under root and says what it did not check.

THE CALLERS MUST CHANGE AS WELL, OR THE NEW STATUS REACHES NOBODY. Four read these functions inside a heredoc, where a failing command substitution is invisible and the loop simply sees a shorter list: publish_install (`$(vendored_paths "$srcroot")`, lib/install:244), manifest_write (:688), vendor_states through vendored_dir_files (:931), and the project vendoring loop in lib/cmd/install (:343). Each is to read the list into a variable, stop on its status, and then loop over it. Only vendor_states' own read of vendored_paths (lib/install:867) checks today, and lib/cmd/upgrade:283 relies on errexit.

RELATED, AND NOT IN THIS FIX: _sha256_of_set (lib/install:700) ends `(cd "$root" && sha256_files ...)` and then `return 0`, so a checksum run that fails reads as success too. Its callers include manifest_check, which doctor runs, and a new failure status there would end doctor the way 0120 did. So giving it a status needs each caller's handling decided first, and that is its own change.

AND IT BEARS ON 0123. 0123's fix makes publish delete what the install holds and the source no longer ships, and it decides "no longer ships" from vendored_paths. Publish is refused today when the source cannot be read, by the seam line above, so that deletion is not exposed through that path. Reading the list with its status inside publish_install means the deletion does not depend on another gate staying in front of it. So this lands with 0123.

The same review found three more swallowed statuses in doctor, none of them reachable today:
- lib/cmd/doctor:237 and :366 count with `grep -c . || true`. The `|| true` is there because grep exits 1 on a zero count, but no comment says so, and it would swallow an exit 2 just as quietly.
- lib/cmd/doctor:400 is `run="$(builtin_option_run "$cmd" "$opt" 2>/dev/null || true)"` in _shadow_hits. It guards a failure the catalogue reader cannot have today. If the reader ever can fail, an overridden @builtin option drops out of the shadow report while doctor says no project name stands where devbin ships its own.

## Resolution

Fixed at c585f3d, in 0123's commit. Ships in 0.1.8.

- WHAT CHANGED. find's output is read whole with its status, through one helper that vendored_paths and vendored_dir_files share, and its error stays on stderr. All seven reads of the vendored set in lib/ check their status, and a class scan in contract.bats fails any read that does not. `install --into` and `upgrade --from` refuse a source find cannot read, naming find's error, where they vendored 45 of 60 files at rc 0 or exited 1 saying nothing. doctor FAILs by name when it cannot list lib/.
- RED FIRST AND MUTANTS. Each arm was red at 0113's landing. V1-V10 were killed, one per status read, the helper, doctor's check, the removal, its pruning and its report. The class scan's first cut accepted `|| :` and let four through; tightened, it kills all four.
- THE SUITE. As 0123's resolution: 1..1694, 1694 ok, 0 not ok, 5 expected skips, rc 0.
